bib.title: An Empirical Study of GPT-3 for Few-Shot Knowledge-Based VQA

question: Can a frozen GPT-3, given images as captions or tags and a few in-context examples, answer knowledge-based VQA without explicit knowledge retrieval or fine-tuning?
hypothesis: GPT-3 acts as an implicit unstructured knowledge base, so prompting it with textual image descriptions unifies knowledge retrieval and reasoning and can beat two-step supervised methods.
contributions: PICa: GPT-3 for knowledge-based VQA, the first use of GPT-3 for multimodal tasks
Images as text, plus in-context example selection and multi-query ensemble
48.0% on OK-VQA few-shot vs 39.4% supervised SOTA; decent few-shot VQAv2

method.summary: Images are converted offline to captions (VinVL-base) and optionally tags (Azure API); a prompt with a fixed head, n in-context VQA examples (caption, question, answer) and the test item is sent to frozen GPT-3, which generates the answer. PICa-Full adds CLIP-similarity example selection and a k-prompt multi-query ensemble choosing the highest summed log-probability answer.

datasets.name: OK-VQA
datasets.size: 14,055 image-question pairs; 5 ground-truth answers per question
datasets.split: test set; in-context examples drawn from an example pool (training set, inferred)

datasets.name: Conceptual Captions
datasets.source: Sharma et al. 2018, used to train VinVL-Caption-CC

models.name: GPT-3
models.architecture: decoder-only LM, frozen, accessed via API

other.variant: inferred: not stated which GPT-3 engine; 175B per Table 1

models.name: VinVL-base captioner
models.init_from: pre-trained VinVL-base checkpoint, fine-tuned on COCO 2014 train (or trained on Conceptual Captions)

other.use: cosine similarity of question text and image features for example selection; RoBERTa compared

models.name: Frozen
models.architecture: GPT-like LM with trained visual encoder

inference.decoding: open-ended text generation, yt = argmax p(yt | C, x, y<t) (greedy as written); stop at EOS
inference.samples: n in-context examples (0 to 16); k prompts per question in ensemble (1, 3, 5); single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Prompt head 'Please answer the question according to the above context.', then n examples 'Context: <caption> Q: <question> A: <answer>', then test 'Context: ... Q: ... A:'. Examples re-selected shorter if prompt exceeds 2049 tokens.
inference.retrieval: in-context example selection: average of CLIP ViT-B/16 question text cosine similarity and image similarity; top n (or n*k) examples; PICa-Base uses random examples

parameters.k: 1,3,5 prompts in multi-query ensemble; n*k examples split over k prompts
parameters.answer_pick: highest sum_t log p(y_t) across k answers

other.rationale_prompt: question + predicted answer + 'This is because', zero-shot

metrics.name: VQAv2 soft accuracy
metrics.definition: soft accuracy against 5 (OK-VQA) ground-truth answers per question

eval.protocol: single reported number per setting, no seeds or confidence intervals stated

limits: Image abstracted as text: captions or tags only partially describe the image and miss visual details such as colour and counts (VQAv2 failures, Fig 4).
Authors expect end-to-end vision encoder tuning would help detail questions.
GPT-3 raw model inaccessible, so behaviour analysis is limited to prompted rationales.
Open-ended answers make evaluation hard (answer-format disagreements).
The best captioner is fine-tuned on COCO 2014 train, which shares the image source with OK-VQA test (COCO val); the CC variant addresses this.
Decoding temperature, max tokens, and GPT-3 engine are not stated; single runs, no variance reported.
All images are COCO photos; no charts or documents.
